titre: Casanova: One Hundred Forty Years of Memoirs No One Could Check
accroche: From 1822 to 1960, five hundred editions of Casanova's Memoirs circulate without any referring to the original manuscript, which remained private.
contenu_vulgarise:
## A Manuscript Sold, Then Erased

Giacomo Casanova dies in May 1798, leaving to his nephew Carlo Angiolini the manuscript of *Histoire de ma vie* (*History of My Life*), written mostly from 1789 and revised from 1794 at the request of the Prince de Ligne, who wished to read it. In 1821, Angiolini's children sell this manuscript to the German publisher Brockhaus, of Leipzig. The text, for its part, does not follow the same path: from 1822, under the title *Mémoires de Casanova* (*Casanova's Memoirs*), some five hundred editions follow one another, none referring to the original manuscript, which remained in the private hands of the Brockhaus family. The French Ministry of Culture, in 2010, would sum up this period with a sober phrase: the text “went through many avatars,” one hundred forty years of expurgated or revised adaptations.

## A Complete Text, but Still Out of Reach

The manuscript, 3,700 pages covered with erasures and entire passages crossed out by Casanova himself, narrowly escapes the bombings of the Second World War. It is not until 1960 that Brockhaus, together with the French publisher Plon, at last publishes a complete edition in French. But the original manuscript remains the private property of a family of publishers, inaccessible to researchers wanting to establish a critical edition. It is only in 2010 that it changes status: on February 18, Minister Frédéric Mitterrand signs with the heirs the contract for its entry into the collections of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (National Library of France), the most important heritage acquisition the institution has ever made, financed entirely by a patron who remained anonymous, under the 2003 patronage law.

## What the Acquisition Changes

Before 2010, no reader, no researcher could compare a printed text of Casanova with the hand that had written it: the five hundred editions copied one another, at a distance from a private and inaccessible original. The Ministry of Culture itself notes in its press release: study of the document “will make it possible to reconstruct the genesis of the work, whose critical edition remains to be established.” What a patron's money changed, in 2010, is therefore not Casanova's text (it has not moved since the 18th century) but the possibility, for the first time since its sale in 1821, of checking it.

repere.texte: The 3,700-page manuscript of Histoire de ma vie, sold in 1821 to the publisher Brockhaus, enters the collections of the Bibliothèque nationale de France only on February 18, 2010: the most important heritage acquisition by the institution, financed entirely by a patron who remained anonymous.
repere.source: Ministry of Culture and Communication, press release, February 18, 2010

carte.punch: For 140 years, no one could check Casanova's real text.
carte.idee: From 1822 to 1960, five hundred editions of Casanova's Memoirs circulate without any referring to the original manuscript, sold in 1821 and kept private. The Bibliothèque nationale de France acquires it only in 2010, finally in a position, for the first time, to check it.

quiz.question: Why can the five hundred editions of Casanova's Memoirs published between 1822 and 1960 not be checked against the original?
choix: Because the original manuscript remained the private property of the family of its first buyer
Because the manuscript had been destroyed in the bombings of the Second World War
Because Casanova himself had forbidden any publication during his lifetime
Because no French publisher had translation rights before 1960
quiz.explication: Sold in 1821 to the publisher Brockhaus, the manuscript remains private until 2010: the successive editions copy one another, with no access to the original.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the Bibliothèque nationale de France's acquisition of the manuscript in 2010 change?
choix: It reveals that Casanova is not the real author of the text
It makes it possible to recover previously unknown chapters
It makes possible, for the first time, a critical edition based on the original
It ends a lawsuit between France and Germany over ownership of the text
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Ministry of Culture notes, in its press release of February 18, 2010, that study of the manuscript will make it possible to establish the critical edition of the text, which remained to be done.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How did the original manuscript nearly vanish before reaching the BnF?
choix: It was stolen and then resold at auction to an anonymous collector
It nearly was destroyed in the bombings of the Second World War
It partly burned in the fire at the Brockhaus printing house in 1900
It was lost during the move of the Brockhaus archives to Paris
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Ministry of Culture's press release states that the manuscript “nearly disappeared in the bombings of the Second World War.”
